Expected a path like "${example}".` - For invalid: `Invalid story path "${value}" for @story annotation. Expected a path like "${example}".` - `buildReqErrorMessage(kind, value, options)`: - Uses `options.reqExample || getDefaultReqExample()`. - For missing: `Missing requirement ID for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like "${example}" (uppercase letters, numbers, and dashes only).` - Because `storyExample` and `reqExample` are derived from nested/flat options with defaults, custom example strings propagate correctly into error text.

traceability.notes: The `valid-annotation-format` rule supports configurable regex patterns and example strings for both @story paths and @req identifiers, via both nested (story/req) and flat (storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern, plus example fields) options. Invalid regex configurations are validated and reported through a dedicated `invalidRuleConfiguration` diagnostic, while the rule safely falls back to its original hardcoded patterns, preserving backward compatibility. Error messages incorporate the configured example strings, and all options are described and constrained via JSON Schema. Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts explicitly cover nested vs flat configuration, example override behavior, invalid regex fallback, and precedence rules, and all tests pass. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md describes these options and provides concrete configuration examples that align with the story. Together, this provides concrete evidence that all acceptance criteria and detailed requirements for 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS are fully implemented.
